column1: # Phiegg's mark, as the picture given on 23 November 2026 has it
# (public/logo/phiegg-icon-drawing.png): a Phi-Pill stem with round ends and its pill
# cut out of it, and two wings, each a quarter of a ring closed by a
# thin bar; the whole leant 45 degrees. The second half is the first
# turned about the middle, as the picture's is, dot for dot.
# name
# Every length is a share of the stem's width, so the mark is drawn at
# any size from these alone. Each number is the picture's own, found by
# laying the drawing over the picture and moving each measure until
# the fewest dots differ: 79 of its 1,647 dots, all at the edges, and
# no edge further than nine tenths of a dot of the picture from it.
# scripts/logo-mark.py --check lays one over the other again.
# How far the mark leans, in degrees, anticlockwise.
lean
# How much of the picture is left clear round the mark.
room
# A wing's ring: the radius of its circle, and how far that circle's
# middle is aside from the stem's own. The stem is as long as the ring
# is wide, so the stem's top runs flat into the top of the wing.
ring
aside
# The bar that closes a wing: where its lower and its upper edge are,
# down from the middle of the mark. It is thin, a sixth of the stem.
bar.low
bar.top
# How thick the ring is at its top, and where the middle of the
# opening's arc is from the ring's own, aside and down: the ring thins
# toward its point, as the picture's does.
band
band.aside
band.down
# Where a wing's opening meets the stem, from the stem's middle. Half a
# stem would be the stem's own side; the picture has it a little in.
inner
# The pill cut out of the stem: how wide and how long, as the picture
# has it. The font's own pill, a third of its stem, is not used: the
# user's word on 23 November 2026, "ignore the font".
pill
pill.long
# How round each corner is: a wing's point, the notch where a bar
# leaves the stem, and an opening's three corners (at the stem's top,
# at the bar, and at the point, which is sharp).
round.tip
round.notch
round.stem
round.bar
round.point
# The picture's own ink, for the sheet; the mark itself takes the
# colour of the text round it.
ink
# In a browser's tab there is no text round it to take a colour from:
# the tab's file has an ink for a light tab and one for a dark tab.
tab.ink
# A tab is 16 dots: there the mark has next to no room left round it,
# so that its pill and openings are as large as they can be.
tab.room
tab.ink.dark
# Where the site keeps the mark: the file with its data, the key under
# `brand` there, and the files written (under public/).
site
site.key
site.file
site.tab
